chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Muaz ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Kindness is a bounty and infringement is an evil omen.

key_terms.الرِّفْقُ: Kindness, gentleness, or ease in conduct
key_terms.الْخُرْقُ: Infringement, defectiveness, or lack of finesse in behavior
key_terms.شُؤْمٌ: Evil omen, misfortune, or ill portent

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of kindness versus infringement in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the metaphysical weight of interpersonal conduct, where الرفق (gentleness) is not merely a social courtesy but a conduit for divine blessing (يمن), while الخرق (harshness or abruptness) invites spiritual misfortune (شؤم). In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the Imams' emphasis on refining character (akhlaq) as a prerequisite for spiritual proximity, reflecting the Prophet's own gentle demeanor in the Quran. It serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate ease in dealings, mirroring the divine attribute of Leniency.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bi Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Muaz Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The kindness is a Bounty and the infringement is an evil omen’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahab from Mu’adh ibn Muslim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Friendliness is a blessing and detachment is evil.’”
